sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to this special edition of The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听本期《一切皆历史》特别节目。

sentences.en: It's Sunday morning, the American presidential election has reached its climax, and last night, among considerable recrimination from Donald Trump,
sentences.zh: 现在是周日早晨，美国总统大选已进入白热化阶段，就在昨晚，在唐纳德·特朗普的一片激烈指责声中，

sentences.en: Joe Biden was declared the 46th president of the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登被宣布为美利坚合众国的第46任总统。

sentences.en: It was an election for the very soul of modern America, with Trump fighting tooth and nail to cling on to power.
sentences.zh: 这是一场争夺现代美国灵魂深处的选举，特朗普为了死死抓住权力进行了拼死搏斗。

sentences.en: So is this unheard of?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种情况史无前例吗？

sentences.en: Who does Trump think he is?
sentences.zh: 特朗普自以为他是谁？

sentences.en: Is he a modern-day Julius Caesar or an updated and slightly shop-soiled Richard Nixon?
sentences.zh: 他是当代的尤利乌斯·恺撒，还是一个略显过时的升级版理查德·尼克松？

sentences.en: Ancient or modern?
sentences.zh: 是古代的还是现代的？

sentences.en: Well, the joke is, of course, that Trump brought the news that Biden had been elected while he was on the golf course, so there have been lots of comments
sentences.zh: 好吧，当然，搞笑的是，特朗普得知拜登当选时他正在打高尔夫球，所以有很多评论

sentences.en: about dictators being cornered in bunkers.
sentences.zh: 都在议论独裁者被逼入地堡。

sentences.en: The Hitler parallel has been much aired, but isn't one, I think, Dominic, that you would have much time for?
sentences.zh: 关于希特勒的类比被广为讨论，不过多米尼克，这恐怕不是你会认同的类比吧？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 大概不会。

sentences.en: But the jokesmith who's just spoken is, of course, my aspiring partner, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 但刚刚发表高论的这位说笑高手，当然就是我雄心勃勃的搭档汤姆·霍兰。

sentences.en: The Trump-Hitler analogy, my goodness, that's a well-worn analogy, and one for which I have absolutely no time at all.
sentences.zh: 特朗普与希特勒的类比，天哪，这都老生常谈了，我压根儿不屑一顾。

sentences.en: Actually, one thing that Trump and Hitler had in common, two things they had in common, Tom.
sentences.zh: 说真的，特朗普和希特勒有一个共同点，汤姆，准确地说有两个共同点。

sentences.en: They're both very funny about their food.
sentences.zh: 他们对吃的东西都非常挑剔。

sentences.en: So Hitler, of course, was a vegetarian, and Trump only eats McDonald's burgers.
sentences.zh: 所以，希特勒当然是个素食主义者，而特朗普只吃麦当劳汉堡。

sentences.en: And they're both very lazy, so Hitler didn't get up until kind of midday and didn't do any work, and I don't think Donald Trump's work ethic has ever really...
sentences.zh: 而且他们都很懒，希特勒差不多到中午才起床，什么活也不干，我觉得唐纳德·特朗普的敬业精神也从来没真的……

sentences.en: And was Hitler teetotal?
sentences.zh: 而且希特勒滴酒不沾吗？

sentences.en: Yes, he was.
sentences.zh: 是的，他不喝酒。

sentences.en: So Trump is as well.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普也是。

sentences.en: So there's a third comparison.
sentences.zh: 这就有了第三个对比。

sentences.en: It's Trump teetotal.
sentences.zh: 那就是特朗普也滴酒不沾。

sentences.en: So they're stacking up.
sentences.zh: 所以相似点越来越多了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Hitler was less orange.
sentences.zh: 希特勒没那么橘红。

sentences.en: Hitler was less orange, no doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 希特勒没那么橘红，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And not into golf, as far as I know.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，他也不喜欢打高尔夫。

sentences.en: OK, OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: So I think that we're really pushing the boundaries of historical inquiry here.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我们在这里真的是在挑战历史研究的边界了。

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But Dominic, actually, talking of historical inquiry, I'm right, aren't I, that Nixon was a particular area of specialisation for you.
sentences.zh: 不过多米尼克，说起历史研究，我没记错的话，尼克松是你的专长领域吧。

sentences.en: That's kind of the area you did your doctorate in.
sentences.zh: 那差不多是你攻读博士学位的领域。

sentences.en: Well, I did my doctorate in sort of late 60s American politics, and that's Richard Nixon's time.
sentences.zh: 对，我读博士研究的是差不多60年代末的美国政治，那正是理查德·尼克松的时代。

sentences.en: So the election in 1968, that's when Nixon, running as a law and order candidate,
sentences.zh: 所以在1968年的大选中，当时尼克松作为奉行法律与秩序的候选人，

sentences.en: carried all before him, and he became US president.
sentences.zh: 一路过关斩将，成为了美国总统。

sentences.en: And I used to teach a course that lasted all year about Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 我过去常常讲授一门持续一整年的关于理查德·尼克松的课程。

sentences.en: It was my special subject course.
sentences.zh: 那是我的专业专题课。

sentences.en: And it was brilliant.
sentences.zh: 而且非常精彩。

sentences.en: We kind of got into Nixon's head.
sentences.zh: 我们算是走进了尼克松的内心世界。

sentences.en: We started with his love letters to Pat, his wife, and we ended with him basically being winched out of the White House, kicking and screaming.
sentences.zh: 我们从他写给妻子帕特的爱情情书开始，到他基本上被拖着踢打尖叫着弄出白宫结束。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is the parallel, because, you know, he's the only analogy I can think of, of somebody leaving the White House with this sort of air of shambolic indignity
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是相似之处，因为，你知道的，他是我能想到的唯一一个离开白宫时带着那种混乱不堪的屈辱感的人，

sentences.en: that we have right now with Mr. Trump.
sentences.zh: 就像我们现在看到的特朗普先生一样。

sentences.en: And Nixon, of course, did not lose an election.
sentences.zh: 而且尼克松当然没有输掉选举。

sentences.en: No, he's an election winner.
sentences.zh: 没错，他是选举的赢家。

sentences.en: Massive winner.
sentences.zh: 大获全胜的赢家。

sentences.en: He's an election winner, so he essentially has to resign.
sentences.zh: 他是选举的赢家，所以他本质上是被迫辞职的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Did he fight to stay in the White House as furiously as Trump is currently fighting?
sentences.zh: 他像现在的特朗普那样拼死挣扎着想要留在白宫吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I suppose he did.
sentences.zh: 对，我想他确实挣扎过。

sentences.en: So it's an extraordinary story, the Nixon story.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非同寻常的故事，尼克松的故事。

sentences.en: It's much more complicated than the Trump story, because Nixon won the 1972 presidential election in a stonking landslide.
sentences.zh: 它比特朗普的故事复杂得多，因为尼克松在1972年的总统大选中以压倒性优势大获全胜。

sentences.en: So there's a big contrast, though, with Trump.
sentences.zh: 所以这与特朗普形成了巨大的反差。

sentences.en: Nixon won every single state except Massachusetts and the District of Columbia.
sentences.zh: 尼克松赢得了除了马萨诸塞州和哥伦比亚特区之外的所有州。

sentences.en: So there's a sort of utter wipeout of the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 因此可以说对民主党是一场彻底的横扫。

sentences.en: But Nixon's gnawing insecurity was such that he had got his team effectively to bug the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但尼克松根深蒂固的不安全感导致他让团队实际去窃听民主党。

sentences.en: He colluded in and then he covered it up and then he covered up the cover up.
sentences.zh: 他串通窃听，然后进行掩盖，接着又掩盖这一掩盖行为。

sentences.en: And so you had this unfolding scandal for the next sort of 18 months or so.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的大约18个月里，这桩丑闻不断发酵。

sentences.en: And when it turned out that Nixon had been taping himself and his sort of dirty secrets were aired before the American public, he had to go.
sentences.zh: 当事实证明尼克松一直在给自己录音，他那些见不得人的秘密被公之于众时，他不得不下台了。

sentences.en: But of course, as politicians always do, he fought and he, you know, he sort of tried everything.
sentences.zh: 但当然，正如政客们一贯的做法那样，他进行了抗争，你知道的，他尝试了一切手段。

sentences.en: He tried to spin things.
sentences.zh: 他试图粉饰太平。

sentences.en: And eventually in August 1974, he, the Republican senators told him, you know, time's up and he had to go.
sentences.zh: 最终在1974年8月，参议院的共和党同僚告诉他，你知道的，时间到了，他必须离开。

sentences.en: But where I think the parallel works is that, you know, Nixon left in the most undignified way possible.
sentences.zh: 但我认为相似之处在于，你知道的，尼克松以极其屈辱的方式离开了。

sentences.en: So he gave a fairly standard resignation speech to the nation.
sentences.zh: 所以他向全国发表了一篇相当常规的辞职演讲。

sentences.en: But when it came to the day of his departure, so the morning of his departure, he stayed up all night sort of sweating and staring into the shadows.
sentences.zh: 但到了他离开的那一天，也就是他离开的那个早晨，他整晚没睡，直冒冷汗，凝视着阴影。

sentences.en: And then, and he's knackered and he's overwrought and he's a bit of a bit of a mess.
sentences.zh: 然后，他筋疲力尽、情绪过度紧张，整个人状态糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And he gives this extraordinary farewell speech to his staff, which is televised.
sentences.zh: 他向幕僚发表了一篇非同寻常的告别演讲，并且通过电视播出了。

sentences.en: And anyone, the listeners who've seen the Anthony Hopkins film, Nixon, will probably remember this.
sentences.zh: 任何看过安东尼·霍普金斯主演的电影《尼克松》的听众大概都会记得这一幕。

sentences.en: And he just completely disintegrates on camera.
sentences.zh: 他在镜头前彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: He's talking about his dad, who was a little guy and a common man.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了他的父亲，一个微不足道的小人物和平民。

sentences.en: He says his mother was a saint.
sentences.zh: 他说他的母亲是个圣人。

sentences.en: He basically starts crying when he talks about his mother.
sentences.zh: 当谈到母亲时，他基本上开始哭泣。

sentences.en: And it's just this awful disintegration and flies completely in the face of everything Americans expect from their president,
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场糟糕透顶的崩溃，完全背离了美国人对总统的一切期待，

sentences.en: which is a level of dignity and civility and sort of sobriety and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 那就是保持一定程度的尊严、礼节、清醒以及诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: And it's sort of gone down as the the acme of what not to do, how not to leave the White House.
sentences.zh: 这被记为反面教材的极致，展示了如何不该离开白宫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's interesting because, I mean, one of the things, of course, that Trump's behavior raises is the question of why do people find it so shocking?
sentences.zh: 这就很有意思了，我的意思是，特朗普的行为引发的一个问题当然是，为什么人们会觉得如此震惊？

sentences.en: And why did people find Nixon's behavior so shocking?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们会觉得尼克松的行为如此震惊？

sentences.en: And it suggests that there is a kind of very strong, often unwritten code about how Americans expect their politicians and particularly their leaders to behave.
sentences.zh: 这表明存在一种非常强烈、通常不成文的准则，关于美国人期望他们的政客、尤其是他们的领导人应该如何行为。

sentences.en: And, of course, this so often goes against the reality, because I guess to reach the top of American politics, you have to play hard and dirty.
sentences.zh: 当然，这往往与现实背道而驰，因为我猜要想登上美国政治的巅峰，你必须手段高明且冷酷无情。

sentences.en: But there is a kind of always this sense that, you know, there are moral standards that you have to live up to.
sentences.zh: 但人们始终有一种感觉，你知道的，有一些你必须遵守的道德标准。

sentences.en: And if, as Trump's currently doing and as Nixon did, you break that, then people are genuinely shocked.
sentences.zh: 如果像特朗普目前所做的那样以及尼克松所做的那样，你打破了这一点，人们就会真的感到震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right, actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, they do fight hard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实在激烈竞争。

sentences.en: But actually, when you look back at American politics, the striking thing is how often they do feel the need to conform to these codes.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，当你回顾美国政治时，最引人注目的是他们是多么频繁地觉得有必要遵守这些准则。

sentences.en: So Al Gore, when he lost the presidency to George Bush and George W.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔·戈尔在2000年将总统宝座输给乔治·布什和乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush in 2000, in kind of dubious circumstances, he behaved in a very, you know, Roman way.
sentences.zh: 布什时，在某种程度上可以说是相当可疑的情况下，他的表现非常，你知道的，很有罗马风范。

sentences.en: He...
Ah.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a gift to you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 哦，汤姆，这简直是送分题啊。

sentences.en: I'll never speak again in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我再也不会在这个播客里说话了。

sentences.en: He gives the ball away.
sentences.zh: 他把球弄丢了。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实丢了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 对，太糟糕了。

sentences.en: He loses possession.
sentences.zh: 他失去了控球权。

sentences.en: It's a schoolboy error.
sentences.zh: 这是个低级失误。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is Roman.
sentences.zh: 对，这很罗马。

sentences.en: It is Roman.
sentences.zh: 这确实很罗马。

sentences.en: I'm so glad you brought that up.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你提起这个。

sentences.en: Because, of course, the question of the code, the code of honour.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，关于准则的问题，荣誉准则。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, it goes back, ultimately, to the, I guess, to the example of Washington.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，归根结底，这可以追溯到华盛顿的榜样。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I'm glad you brought it back to American politics, Tom, and left the Romans behind.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你把话题拉回了美国政治，汤姆，把罗马人抛在了脑后。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, well, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，等等，等等。

sentences.en: Because Washington is a general.
sentences.zh: 因为华盛顿是一位将军。

sentences.en: He's a victorious general who has thrown out a king and who has laboured to establish a republic.
sentences.zh: 他是一位功勋卓著的将军，推翻了一位国王，并为建立共和国付出了艰辛努力。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so the big question is, you know, is he going to lay down his sword?
sentences.zh: 所以最大的问题是，你知道的，他会交出指挥权吗？

sentences.en: Is he going to return to his farm?
sentences.zh: 他会返回他的农场吗？

sentences.en: And it so happens that the American founding fathers, who are absolutely steeped in the study of ancient Roman history, have the model of the Roman Republic to hand.
sentences.zh: 恰巧的是，对古罗马历史有着极深研究的美国国父们，手头现成就有罗马共和国的模版。

sentences.en: Because the Roman Republic is established after a king is expelled.
sentences.zh: 因为罗马共和国是在驱逐国王后建立的。

sentences.en: And it works because it establishes this code, the Mos Maior, when they call them, the kind of the customs held to by the ancestors that everyone is expected to hold to.
sentences.zh: 它的运转之所以成功，是因为它确立了这样一种准则，即他们所说的“先辈风俗”（Mos Maior），也就是每个人都被期望坚守的祖传习俗。

sentences.en: And that's what the founding fathers are kind of looking to.
sentences.zh: 这就是国父们所期望效仿的。

sentences.en: And that's the model that Washington is drawing on.
sentences.zh: 这也是华盛顿所借鉴的模版。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So the Washington story is a good one.
sentences.zh: 所以华盛顿的故事是个好故事。

sentences.en: So he basically gives up his command in 1783.
sentences.zh: 他基本上在1783年放弃了他的指挥权。

sentences.en: The Continental Army has won, or rather the French have won the war for them.
sentences.zh: 大陆军赢得了胜利，或者更准确地说，法国人帮他们赢得了战争。

sentences.en: Britain has basically given up.
sentences.zh: 英国人基本上放弃了。

sentences.en: America has its independence.
sentences.zh: 美国获得了独立。

sentences.en: And actually, there's then a six-year break before Washington actually becomes president.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在此之后还有六年的间歇期，华盛顿才真正成为总统。

sentences.en: So he doesn't actually become president until 1789.
sentences.zh: 所以他直到1789年才真正当上总统。

sentences.en: And basically, they have to drag him kicking and screaming into the job.
sentences.zh: 基本上，人们是连拉带拽、连踢带叫地把他弄进这个职位的。

sentences.en: He doesn't really want to do it.
sentences.zh: 他其实并不想干。

sentences.en: They turn to him because he's a unifying figure, because he's a patriotic figure and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 大家推选他是因为他是一个具有凝聚力的人物，因为他是一个爱国人物以及诸如此类的原因。

sentences.en: But he doesn't really fancy it.
sentences.zh: 但他其实并不太热衷。

sentences.en: And then after his first term, again, he doesn't really want to carry on.
sentences.zh: 而在他的第一个任期结束后，同样地，他并不真的想继续干下去。

sentences.en: And they basically compel him.
sentences.zh: 基本上是大家硬逼着他。

sentences.en: The other founding fathers say, no, no, you must stay and do it.
sentences.zh: 其他国父们说，不，不，你必须留下来干完。

sentences.en: And then he leaves after his second term and establishes this tradition, which only one president, FDR, in the Second World War, has ever broken,
sentences.zh: 然后他在第二个任期结束后离任，并确立了这样一条传统——历史上只有罗斯福总统在二战期间打破过一次——

sentences.en: that a president will only do two terMs.
sentences.zh: 那就是总统只能担任两届。

sentences.en: So that sort of – I'm hesitant to give you the ball back so easily.
sentences.zh: 所以那种——我很犹豫是不是该这么轻易地把球还给你。

sentences.en: But that sort of ethos of the reluctant leader who has to be sort of coerced into the job.
sentences.zh: 但那种不情愿的领导人的精神风貌，不得不被某种程度上胁迫着去承担这份工作。

sentences.en: I mean, he's obviously trying to live up – I mean, he was the president of a group called the Society of the Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他显然在极力践行——我的意思是，他是辛辛纳提学会这个组织的会长。

sentences.en: And there you have your Roman hero, Cincinnatus, that I'm sure you're about to tell us about.
sentences.zh: 瞧，你心中的罗马英雄辛辛纳提这不就来了，我确信你正准备跟我们讲讲他呢。

sentences.en: I certainly have.
sentences.zh: 我当然要讲。

sentences.en: So Cincinnatus is absolutely the archetype for this, who is a legendary figure from the early years of the Roman Republic.
sentences.zh: 所以辛辛纳提绝对是这方面的典型代表，他是罗马共和国早期的一位传奇人物。

sentences.en: And the reason that he serves as such an iconic figure, both for the Romans and then for the Americans, is that he's a great war leader who is also a farmer.
sentences.zh: 他之所以能成为罗马人乃至后来美国人心中如此具有标志性的人物，是因为他既是一位伟大的军事领袖，又是一位农民。

sentences.en: And he is summoned from his plough to save his people, to lead his country.
sentences.zh: 他从犁头旁被召唤出来拯救他的同胞，领导他的国家。

sentences.en: And then having saved his country, he then returns to the plough.
sentences.zh: 然后在拯救了国家之后，他又回到了犁头旁。

sentences.en: And this is such a kind of perfect image for Washington.
sentences.zh: 这简直是华盛顿最完美的写照。

sentences.en: There's a sensational statue.
sentences.zh: 史密森尼博物馆里有一尊轰动一时的雕像。

sentences.en: I think it's in the Smithsonian by Horatio Greenough, which obviously this is a podcast, so unfortunately I can't bring it up for you.
sentences.zh: 我想那是霍雷肖·格里诺的作品，显然这是一个播客，所以很遗憾我没法把它展示给你们看。

sentences.en: But anyone, Google it.
sentences.zh: 但大家可以去谷歌一下。

sentences.en: It's so brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太绝了。

sentences.en: It's Washington with his wig in a toga, holding a sword.
sentences.zh: 那是戴着假发、身穿托加袍、手握长剑的华盛顿。

sentences.en: And it perfectly illustrates this kind of strange 18th century Roman fusion that the early American Republic kind of absolutely plays with.
sentences.zh: 它完美地诠释了早期美利坚共和国那种奇特的18世纪罗马融合风，这也是他们当时绝对乐于把玩的元素。

sentences.en: So those early Americans, I mean, they basically thought they were the Romans, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 所以那些早期的美国人，我的意思是，他们基本上觉得自己就是罗马人，对吧？

sentences.en: But particular kind of Romans, right?
sentences.zh: 但指的是某种特定的罗马人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because obviously there's lots of, they have this, do they have this idealised image of Rome, do you think?
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，很多人对罗马有一种理想化的形象，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously most Romans are probably just like us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然大多数罗马人可能和我们差不多。

sentences.en: Yes, they're haunted by the fact that, of course, the early days of the Republic, when everyone is virtuous and kind of yeoman farmers and at their plough,
sentences.zh: 是的，他们深知并萦绕在一个事实中，那就是共和国的早期，每个人都品德高尚，有点像自耕农，躬耕于田亩之间，

sentences.en: that the Roman Republic expands, it becomes incredibly wealthy, it becomes a superpower, it establishes its rule across the whole of the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 罗马共和国不断扩张，变得极其富有，成为超级大国，将其统治确立到整个地中海。

sentences.en: And this then provides opportunities for ambitious Roman politicians to put the entire Republic in its shadow.
sentences.zh: 这随后为雄心勃勃的罗马政客提供了让整个共和国黯然失色的机会。

sentences.en: And in due course, that results in the establishment of an autocracy.
sentences.zh: 久而久之，这就导致了独裁政权的建立。

sentences.en: And so every founding father is nervously aware of this.
sentences.zh: 因此，每一位国父都对此心怀戒备。

sentences.en: And so Benjamin Franklin, when he comes, he says, you know, is it going to be a Republic?
sentences.zh: 所以本杰明·富兰克林来了之后，他说，你知道的，这会是一个共和国吗？

sentences.en: And he says, yeah, it's going to be a Republic if we can keep hold of it.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，如果我们能守住它，它就会是一个共和国。

sentences.en: And that anxiety is always, and I guess it's, it's because, you know, Nixon is very keen on the idea of America as an imperial Republic.
sentences.zh: 这种焦虑一直都在，我想这是因为，你知道的，尼克松非常热衷于将美国视为一个帝制共和国的想法。

sentences.en: And so that's part of the shadow, I would guess, is it, of what's going on with Watergate and people's anxiety about him?
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这也是水门事件以及人们对他的焦虑背后的一部分阴影吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, people talked about the imperial presidency.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，人们谈论过帝王般的总统职权。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你完全说得对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So obviously what had happened, I mean, basically until the 20th century, you know, America was kind of happening.
sentences.zh: 很明显发生的事情是，基本上直到20世纪，你知道的，美国一直在按自己的节奏发展。

sentences.en: But as far as the rest of the world was concerned, it was somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 但就世界其他地方而言，它只是在某个遥远的地方。

sentences.en: Who cared about them?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎他们呢？

sentences.en: Let them get on with it.
sentences.zh: 随他们折腾去吧。

sentences.en: But then the 20th century, America does become an empire.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪，美国确实变成了一个帝国。

sentences.en: I mean, there's people argue about this, but there's no doubt really.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，虽然有人对此争论不休，但其实毫无疑问。

sentences.en: It has colonies.
sentences.zh: 它有殖民地。

sentences.en: It has overseas bases.
sentences.zh: 它有海外基地。

sentences.en: It has influence.
sentences.zh: 它有影响力。

sentences.en: It wins wars in foreign countries.
sentences.zh: 它在外国的战争中获胜。

sentences.en: And the people talk about the president as an American Caesar.
sentences.zh: 人们把总统称为美利坚的凯撒。

sentences.en: They use that sort of terminology.
sentences.zh: 他们使用这种术语。

sentences.en: And Nixon, so the presidencies of LBJ, Lyndon Johnson, who preceded Nixon, who's famous for Vietnam, and then Nixon, who ends the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 尼克松之前，林登·约翰逊（LBJ，因越南战争而闻名）的总统任期，然后是结束越战的尼克松。

sentences.en: That's kind of the high point of what people think of as the imperial presidency, of a president that can do what he wants.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是人们所认为的帝王式总统职权的巅峰，即总统可以为所欲为。

sentences.en: He can evade who he wants.
sentences.zh: 他可以逃避任何他想逃避的人。

sentences.en: He's accumulating more and more power.
sentences.zh: 他积累了越来越多的权力。

sentences.en: And certainly in Nixon's case, he's using people like the FBI to, you know, survey his opponents, to bug his opponents.
sentences.zh: 当然，就尼克松而言，他利用联邦调查局（FBI）这样的人来监视政敌，窃听政敌。

sentences.en: There's this sort of fear, which now seems completely hysterical, but at the time was very real in the early 1970s, that, you know, under Nixon,
sentences.zh: 当时在20世纪70年代初，有一种现在看起来完全歇斯底里但在当时却非常真实的恐惧，那就是在尼克松的统治下，

sentences.en: America was turning into a sort of police state.
sentences.zh: 美国正在变成某种警察国家。

sentences.en: And actually, that's not so different from what we've heard in the last four years from Donald Trump's critics, who believe that he represents the end of the Republican dream.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这跟我们在过去四年里从唐纳德·特朗普的批评者那里听到的并没有太大不同，他们认为特朗普代表着共和党梦想的终结。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, I think that that's been an anxiety that has shadowed the American Republic pretty much from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这也是一种从美利坚共和国建立之初就一直挥之不去的焦虑。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, if you model yourself on Rome, if you have a capital, if you have a Senate, if your capital city has loads of columns and pillars that look like ancient Rome,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，如果你以罗马为模板，如果你有首都，如果你有参议院，如果你的首都到处都是模仿古罗马的圆柱和柱廊，

sentences.en: then there are two things that are going to worry you.
sentences.zh: 那么有两件事会让你担忧。

sentences.en: The first is that if you're a republic, that essentially the republic is going to collapse and that a Caesar is going to emerge in Augustus.
sentences.zh: 第一件是，如果你是一个共和国，本质上共和国将会崩溃，一个类似于屋大维的凯撒将会崛起。

sentences.en: And the second one is that the entire, you know, the Roman Empire fell.
sentences.zh: 第二件是，整个，你知道的，罗马帝国灭亡了。

sentences.en: And so the American Empire will fall.
sentences.zh: 所以美利坚帝国也会灭亡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that those, that's a kind of, although the Hitler, you know, Trump as Hitler has been very, very kind of popular theme over the past four years.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，尽管在过去四年里，把特朗普比作希特勒一直是一个非常非常热门的主题。

sentences.en: I think the Trump as a kind of Caesar has also been pretty popular.
sentences.zh: 我认为把特朗普比作某种凯撒也相当受欢迎。

sentences.en: I know I've made a lot of good money writing farfetched comparisons between Trump and Nero and so on.
sentences.zh: 我知道我通过写一些关于特朗普和尼禄之间牵强附会的对比赚了不少好钱。

sentences.en: People often talk about the drawbacks of the Trump presidency, but they don't mention this one, which is the greatest, which is the immense amount of money you've made out of it.
sentences.zh: 人们经常谈论特朗普总统任期的弊端，但他们没有提到最严重的一点，那就是你从中学到了巨额财富。

sentences.en: Well, not immense amount of money.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也不是巨额财富。

sentences.en: I mean, scratching together the old penny.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，只能算东拼西凑几个旧便士。

sentences.en: But I think that that is a kind of, it's been there right from, say, Andrew Jackson.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这是一种，从安德鲁·杰克逊时期开始就一直存在的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He was a general, a successful general.
sentences.zh: 他是一名将军，一位功勋卓著的将军。

sentences.zh: 1812年战争的将军。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: People start thinking that he's going to be a Caesar.
sentences.zh: 人们开始认为他会成为一个凯撒。

sentences.en: And I think that essentially the, the idea, if you model yourself on Rome, the idea that you're going to decline and fall is kind of hardwired into your, into your mind.
sentences.zh: 我认为本质上，如果你以罗马为模板，这种你会走向衰落和灭亡的想法已经深深烙印在你的脑海中了。

sentences.en: But isn't it odd, Tom, that they keep electing generals, which is kind of a Roman thing in itself.
sentences.zh: 但是托马斯，他们不断选举将军，这本身不是很奇怪吗，这在某种程度上也很罗马化。

sentences.en: So Andrew Jackson is a general, Ulysses Grant after the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 所以安德鲁·杰克逊是一位将军，内战后有尤利西斯·格兰特。

sentences.en: And then even after World War II, they, they go for Eisenhower, you know, the architect of D-Day.
sentences.zh: 甚至在二战之后，他们也选择了艾森豪威尔，你知道的，诺曼底登陆的策划者。

sentences.en: Although what's interesting with Biden, who, who, who, like every other man of his generation, president of his generation, did not serve in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 尽管有趣的是，拜登和他那一代的所有总统一样，并没有在越南服役。

sentences.en: Actually, the key fact about recent presidents is that they didn't serve in the military.
sentences.zh: 事实上，关于近期历任总统的一个关键事实是，他们都没有在军队服役过。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Which is a kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: And the one who did famously fail to win, John McCain.
sentences.zh: 而那个参军的人却没能赢得大选，也就是约翰·麦凯恩。

sentences.en: So John McCain was actually an extraordinarily Roman figure, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以约翰·麦凯恩实际上是一个极其具有罗马色彩的人物，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he's like somebody who's basically decided to role play his entire life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他就像是一个基本上决定了自己一生都在进行角色扮演的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: As a Roman war hero.
sentences.zh: 扮演一个罗马战争英雄。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because he, he, he, he fights for his country.
sentences.zh: 因为他为了国家而战。

sentences.en: He gets captured and brutally tortured and refuses to give in.
sentences.zh: 他被俘虏并遭受了残酷的折磨，但拒绝屈服。

sentences.en: And that, again, is absolutely redolent of, of figures from Roman history.
sentences.zh: 而这，又完全让人联想起罗马历史上的那些人物。

sentences.en: There's this guy, Regulus, who leads a campaign against the Carthaginians in the First Punic War, gets captured, gets sent back to Rome on the proviso that he will sue for terMs.
sentences.zh: 有这么一个人叫雷古鲁斯，在第一次布匿战争中率领军队对抗迦太基，被俘后被遣返回罗马，前提是他要促成和平条款。

sentences.en: And encouraged the Senate to, to basically, to surrender to Carthage.
sentences.zh: 并鼓励参议院基本上向迦太基投降。

sentences.en: Regulus gets back to Rome, refuses to encourage the Senate to surrender, says no, carry on fighting, and then feels honour bound to return to Carthage,
sentences.zh: 雷古鲁斯回到罗马后，拒绝鼓励参议院投降，说不，继续战斗，然后觉得自己有责任回到迦太基，

sentences.en: where he gets put in a barrel that has spikes driven through it.
sentences.zh: 在那里他被塞进一个钉满了尖刺的木桶里。

sentences.en: And he gets rolled down a hill.
sentences.zh: 然后他被人从山上滚下去。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.zh: 那这会要了他的命吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it does kill him.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实要了他的命。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, of course, McCain survives, but, you know, he, he, he, he kind of goes through torture for America in pretty much the same way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，麦凯恩活了下来，但是，你知道的，他为美国经历的折磨也差不多是这样。

sentences.en: And in a way, one of the most kind of shocking things that Trump said, and, and, you know, kind of darkly funny, was he said, I don't like losers.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，特朗普说过的话中最令人震惊且带有一丝黑色幽默的一点是，他说，我不喜欢失败者。
